draft.title: Biome productivity
card: Biome productivity is how much plant matter a biome grows each year. Plants are the base of the food supply for animals in that biome.
Plants need light, warmth and water to grow. Where all three are plentiful, plants grow fast and in large amounts.
Warm, wet biomes such as tropical rainforests grow the most plant matter each year.
Cold or dry biomes grow the least. Tundra is too cold for much of the year, and deserts have very little water.
draft.remember: Plants grow most where it is warm and wet, and least where it is cold or dry.

a.q: Which biome grows the most plant matter each year?
a.why: A tropical rainforest is warm and wet all year, so plants grow fast. Tundra is the most tempting wrong option, but it is too cold for much of the year, so it grows little.
a.clue: Think of the biome with both warmth and water.

b.q: Two regions get similar sunshine. Region X gets heavy rain all year. Region Y is dry with little rain. Which statement about their productivity is best?
opts: X is more productive because it has more water
Y is more productive because dry air gives more light
They match because they get similar sunshine
Y is more productive because plants there grow slowly
b.why: With similar sunshine, water decides the difference. Region X has plenty of water, so its plants grow more each year. Matching sunshine does not make them equal, because plants need water as well as light.
b.clue: Light is equal, so look at what differs.

b.best: X is more productive because it has more water
